COP31: UN Climate summit enters final phase with no deal in sight
November 20, 2026
After nearly two weeks of negotiations, countries remain divided on how to fight global warming. A new draft declaration doesn't mention the phaseout of fossil fuels, the main drivers of climate change. DW has more.
What you need to know
- Diplomats and delegates from nearly 200 countries are meeting in Antalya, Turkey
- A new draft deal omits any mention of how to phase out fossil fuels, in what campaigners call a step 'backwards' and a 'glaring regression'
- Like in previous years, the climate summit is likely to be extended until a consensus is reached
These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20, 2026:
IN DEPTH — Fossil fuels dropped from latest COP31 draft deal
One of the most fraught debates at the UN climate talks in Turkey has revolved around the future of coal, oil and gas.
Now, all mention of fossil fuels has been removed from the summit's new draft agreement.
Learn more about why fossil fuels, the main drivers of global warming, were removed from the COP31 draft declaration in this report.
COP summit poised to be extended with no deal imminent
Delegations from nearly 200 countries have been meeting in the Turkish resort city of Antalya since November 9 to negotiate ways to tackle global warming and provide financial aid to the world's poorest and most vulnerable nations to climate change.
But, as in previous years, countries remain sharply divided, and consensus has proven elusive.
Three years ago, at COP28 in Dubai, nations pledged to move away from fossil fuels, although no target or timeline was ever set.
Oil- and gas-producing countries have strongly resisted attempts to bring that particular issue back to the negotiating table.
Last year's COP30 summit in Brazil concluded with no mention of fossil fuels, prompting some nations to pursue the fight outside of the UN's sphere.
This year's summit is being held against the backdrop of rising living costs and the US-Israeli war with Iran, which has sent shockwaves through global energy markets and sent prices soaring.
Those challenges have taken the focus away from long-standing issues like rising global temperatures and increasingly frequent and extreme weather disasters, which have been exacerbated by this year's record-breaking El Nino.
In an initial draft deal earlier in the week, the phaseout of fossil fuels was included.
But a new draft declaration released on Thursday night by Australia, which is co-hosting the summit, omits any mention of gas, oil and coal, widely recognized as the main drivers of climate change.
The omission is a "black mark," France's Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said.
Climate activists have also slammed what they call a "glaring regression."
"You cannot solve a fossil fuel crisis by pretending we don't need to phase out fossil fuels," said Harjeet Singh, convenor of the Fill the Fund campaign.
The director of Power Shift Africa, Mohamed Adow, also condemned the slimmed-down draft text, which he said had "gone backwards."
Despite the current differences, Australia's Climate Minister Chris Bowen, who is leading negotiations, said, "We will be consulting and negotiating until it is very clear to us that we have a consensus."
IN PICTURES — Hotter seas, more plastic: High stakes for oceans
IN DEPTH — Have we missed our chance on climate?
From record-breaking heat to devastating floods and wildfires, the warning signs are everywhere. Can rising temperatures still be brought under control?
Learn more about whether the world is acting too late to stop catastrophic climate change in this report.
Welcome to our coverage
Thank you for joining us as we bring you live updates from what is scheduled to be the final day of the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Turkey's southern Mediterranean resort city.
Like in previous years, however, it is looking increasingly likely that the negotiations will have to be extended, amid significant differences between delegates despite nearly two weeks of talks.
A new version of a joint draft declaration unveiled on Thursday night omits any mention of how to transition away from fossil fuels — the main causes of global warming.
Stay tuned as we bring you more details on those talks in this blog.
digest_he:
ועידת האקלים COP31 של האו"ם, המתקיימת באנטליה שבטורקיה בהשתתפות נציגים מלמעלה ממאתיים מדינות, נכנסה לשלב הסיום שלה ללא סימנים להסכם מתגבש. המחלוקת המרכזית סובבת סביב עתידם של הפחם, הנפט והגז, כאשר טיוטת ההסכם החדשה שהוצגה על ידי אוסטרליה השמיטה לחלוטין את הדרישה להפסיק את השימוש בדלקים מאובנים.

ההחלטה להסיר את הסעיף עוררה ביקורת חריפה מצד שרים ופעילים סביבתיים, שכינו את המהלך נסיגה חמורה ומדאיגה במאבק נגד משבר האקלים. מדינות המפיקות נפט וגז התנגדו בעוצמה להחזרת הסוגיה לשולחן הדיונים, על רקע אתגרים גלובליים כמו יוקר המחיה והשפעות המלחמה במזרח התיכון על שוקי האנרגיה.

בדומה לשנים קודמות, נציגי המדינות צפויים להאריך את הדיונים בניסיון להגיע לקונצנזוס. למרות הקשיים, שר האקלים האוסטרלי כריס בואן הדגיש כי ההתייעצויות והמשא ומתן יימשכו עד אשר יושג הסכם מוסכם על הכל.
